title: Flood susceptibility with GLO-30 HAND
text: universal cut-turns HAND flood map, sensible threshold depends basin, channel network used derive product return period mind. Values single digits metres usual starting point, result treated screening layer. explore values dplyr, take raster data frame, one row per cell column named hand (na.rm = TRUE drops cells outside boundary):  screening mask single comparison:  Classifying bands often honest binary mask, keeps gradient visible:  bands, counted data frame, give share area :
code: hand_values <- as.data.frame(hand, na.rm = TRUE)  hand_values |>   summarise(     cells = n(),     mean = mean(hand),     p05 = quantile(hand, 0.05),     median = median(hand),     p95 = quantile(hand, 0.95)   ) #>   cells     mean p05   median      p95 #> 1 63390 9.654945   0 6.339997 30.78297 hist(hand_values$hand, breaks = 50,      main = "HAND distribution", xlab = "Metres above nearest drainage") lowland <- hand < 5 plot(lowland, main = "Terrain within 5 m of the nearest drainage") # Share of the municipality below the threshold hand_values |>   summarise(share_below_5m = mean(hand < 5)) #>   share_below_5m #> 1      0.4398959 bands <- matrix(c(    0,  2, 1,   # very low terrain, closest to the channel    2,  5, 2,    5, 15, 3,   15, Inf, 4   # well above the drainage ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)  hand_class <- classify(hand, bands) plot(hand_class, main = "HAND bands") hand_values |>   mutate(band = cut(hand, breaks = c(0, 2, 5, 15, Inf),                     labels = c("0-2 m", "2-5 m", "5-15 m", "> 15 m"),                     include.lowest = TRUE)) |>   count(band) |>   mutate(share = n / sum(n)) #>     band     n     share #> 1  0-2 m 18659 0.2943524 #> 2  2-5 m  9226 0.1455435 #> 3 5-15 m 19747 0.3115160 #> 4 > 15 m 15758 0.2485881

title: Mapping geological risk with the SGB
text: raw layer carries dozen fields, many administrative metadata. Selecting fields matter labelling makes map far easier read: colour combination fields — say risk level process type — build combined category first:
code: library(leafpop)  fields <- c("locality", "process_type", "process_subtype", "risk_level",             "survey_date", "n_people") labels <- c("Locality", "Process", "Specific type", "Risk level",             "Surveyed", "People")  popup_data <- angra |>   select(all_of(setNames(fields, labels)))  mapview(   angra,   zcol = "risk_level",   col.regions = c("Alto" = "#F59E0B", "Muito alto" = "#DC2626"),   map.types = "Esri.WorldImagery",   layer.name = "Risk sectors",   popup = popupTable(popup_data, feature.id = FALSE, row.numbers = FALSE) ) angra <- angra |>   mutate(risk_process = paste(risk_level, process_type, sep = " | "))  mapview(angra, zcol = "risk_process", map.types = "Esri.WorldImagery")

what: An R package for extracting global climate risk, susceptibility, and vulnerability data
title: An R package for extracting global climate risk, susceptibility, and vulnerability data
text: geohazards R package extracting global data related climate risk, susceptibility, vulnerability. provides simple interface accessing remote geospatial datasets (flood susceptibility indices, landslide risk maps, geological hazard layers) directly R, without manual downloading. package currently covers two data sources: GLO-30 HAND, read_hand(), retrieves GLO-30 HAND (Height Nearest Drainage) raster 30 m resolution polygon supplied user. SGB/CPRM, read_sgb() friends, retrieve geological risk cartography published Geological Survey Brazil — risk sectorisation, flood mapping disaster occurrences — plus technical reports deposited repository (RIGeo). actively expanded new data sources functions, planned submission CRAN.

title: An R package for extracting global climate risk, susceptibility, and vulnerability data
text: example retrieves HAND raster municipality São Paulo, Brazil. HAND measures, metres, high point terrain nearest drainage channel, lower values indicate greater flood susceptibility.
code: library(geohazards) library(geobr)  # Look up the IBGE code for São Paulo and download its boundary as an sf object spo_ibge <- lookup_muni("São Paulo")$code_muni spo_geo  <- read_municipality(code_muni = spo_ibge, year = 2022)  # Fetch the HAND raster clipped to the municipality boundary. # Data is read remotely via Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (no full tile downloads). spo_hand <- read_hand(place = spo_geo)  # Visualise the result terra::plot(spo_hand)

text: Two catalogues one function. source = "local" (default) searches IBGE municipality table embedded package, works offline way find code_muni municipality. source = "server" asks SGB municipalities actually risk sectorisation mapped, requires network access.

title: List Brazilian municipalities known to the SGB — sgb_municipalities
code: sgb_municipalities(search = NULL, state = NULL, source = c("local", "server"))

title: List Brazilian municipalities known to the SGB — sgb_municipalities
text: search Optional fragment municipality name. Matching case-insensitive tolerant accents, "petropolis" finds "Petrópolis". state Optional two-letter state abbreviation (e.g. "RJ"). source "local" search embedded IBGE table, "server" list municipalities covered SGB risk sectorisation.

title: List Brazilian municipalities known to the SGB — sgb_municipalities
text: data.frame code_muni, name_muni abbrev_state.

title: List Brazilian municipalities known to the SGB — sgb_municipalities
code: # Offline search of the embedded IBGE table sgb_municipalities(search = "petropolis") #>   code_muni       name_muni abbrev_state #> 1   3303906      Petrópolis           RJ #> 2   4313201 Nova Petrópolis           RS  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   # Municipalities with risk sectorisation mapped by the SGB, in Bahia   sgb_municipalities(state = "BA", source = "server") } # }

what: Catalogue of SGB risk products — sgb_products
title: Catalogue of SGB risk products — sgb_products
text: Lists geological risk layers published Geological Survey Brazil (SGB/CPRM) GeoSGB server, identifier one requested read_sgb(). Four layers listed flagged queryable: exist SGB holdings, yet endpoint answer queries public server. kept catalogue absence documented rather silent.

title: Catalogue of SGB risk products — sgb_products
code: sgb_products()

title: Catalogue of SGB risk products — sgb_products
text: data.frame one row per product columns: product Identifier pass read_sgb(). service Name service SGB server, traceability official documentation. theme Hazard theme covered layer. type "cartography" mapped polygons, "occurrence" reported disaster events. key Attribute layer filtered server. scope "municipality" layers can filtered municipality, "national" point layers carry municipality attribute clipped spatially. queryable Whether SGB server answers queries layer.

title: geohazards 0.2.0
text: get_hand() renamed read_hand(). Functions return data now consistently use read_* prefix.

title: geohazards 0.2.0
text: Access geological risk cartography Geological Survey Brazil (SGB/CPRM), incorporating work Julio Pedrassoli sgbrisco package: read_sgb() downloads risk product (risk sectorisation, flood mapping, disaster occurrences) municipality, state whole country, sf object SIRGAS 2000 (EPSG:4674). sgb_products() lists catalogue SGB products, including four layers exist SGB holdings public server answer queries . sgb_inventory() reports mapped municipality, state whole country, without downloading geometry. sgb_municipalities() searches embedded IBGE municipality table, municipalities SGB actually mapped. read_sgb_report() downloads extracts technical report RIGeo, institutional repository SGB. Field names returned SGB translated English, dates server encodes epoch milliseconds returned Date. original SGB field names documented function’s Value section.

title: geohazards 0.2.0
text: read_sgb() longer returns fields identify people. occurrence layers carry e-mail whoever reported event (email) account name whoever created edited record (created_user, last_edited_user); now dropped page downloaded.
